question: When lung cancer treatments were described by chances of living or of dying, were doctors swayed as much as patients?
answer: Yes. Choosing between surgery and radiation, more people preferred surgery when its outcomes were given as survival rather than mortality, though the numbers were identical. Physicians shifted too, not only patients and students. Training did not protect against wording. A 10% death rate and 90% survival are the same patients.
move: Hear the survival figure and the death figure before choosing.
ask: When I am offered a choice with a percentage, have I heard it both ways round?
reference: McNeil, Pauker, Sox & Tversky, On the elicitation of preferences for alternative therapies, New England Journal of Medicine, 1982
